Stillaguamish

The Stillaguamish Tribe’s own history centers on its river and the north and south forks. Its historical and cultural-department accounts offer a starting path into continuing community relationships, government and the care of cultural knowledge.

03

People remaining with their river

The Tribe’s history describes ancestors living along the Stillaguamish River and both forks. It explains that some families moved to Tulalip while others remained in the river area, and records federal acknowledgement in 1976. This account helps distinguish Stillaguamish continuity from a simple story of relocation or disappearance. Original governmental records remain a separate research task.

Read the sources [1] Stillaguamish Tribe of Indians

04

Archives, landscapes and learning

The Cultural Resources Department’s 2022 account links archive keeping and protection of cultural places with community learning activities, including language workshops. It presents these as responsibilities of a living community institution. The directory has not assessed later programme availability or outcomes, and its public description does not make every cultural record unrestricted.

Read the sources [4] Stillaguamish Tribe of Indians

Our History — Stillaguamish Tribe ↗

The March5,2026-updated account names the Stillaguamish River and both forks, describes families remaining near the river, and narrates governmental acknowledgement. Tracey Boser is credited for its cultural-history section.

Inspection: Content reviewed for the stated scope

Scope: Read complete historical body: introductory paragraphs, Land Acknowledgement Example and Tribal History by Tracey Boser, web lines35–66. Synthesis uses river relationships and the stated 1976 acknowledgement, not precise village sites or restricted practices.

Review recorded: October 28, 2026

Access note: Public source body inspected through the web reader and/or a normal HTTP200 local copy. Linked recordings, original records, objects and photographs were not automatically inspected or licensed. No login, paywall bypass or outreach. Original acknowledgement files, land records and current legal powers were not reviewed. Geological dates, current acreage/totals and ceremonial/medicinal particulars are not adopted. No source photographs copied.

https://www.stillaguamish.com/our-history/

Cultural Resources Department — Stillaguamish Tribe ↗

The January11,2022-updated departmental account describes archive keeping, cultural-landscape protection and community learning activities. It records institutional responsibilities, not measured present outcomes.

Inspection: Content reviewed for the stated scope

Scope: Overview and department functions/activities, web lines35–57. The separate Chief Seattle-attributed quotation is excluded from synthesis and not verified or reproduced.

Review recorded: October 28, 2026

Access note: Public source body inspected through the web reader and/or a normal HTTP200 local copy.
